title: Abelian images and the kernel dimension formula
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $A,B$ be abelian varieties over $k$ [def-sc-abelian-variety], and let $f:A\to B$ be a $k$-group-scheme homomorphism [def-sc-group-scheme]. Its scheme-theoretic image $I\hookrightarrow B$ (the closed subscheme defined by the kernel of $\mathcal O_B\to f_*\mathcal O_A$, as in [lem-sc-image-subgroup]) is an abelian variety over $k$. Writing $K=\ker f$ for the scheme-theoretic kernel, one has $\dim A=\dim I+\dim K$. These are dimensions of finite-type $k$-schemes; no perfectness or separability hypothesis on $k$ or $f$ is required.

source.place: Theorem 1.72 and its proof, printed pp.28–29 (geometrically reduced image from a smooth source); Theorem 5.39 and Remark 5.42, printed pp.108–109 (kernel dimension formula). For proper source the image is proper and connected. Compare Milne AV I Proposition 7.1, printed p.32.

proof.text: Put $j:I\hookrightarrow B$ and $q:A\to I$. By [lem-sc-image-subgroup], $I$ is a finite-type closed subgroup of $B$ and $q$ is surjective. Since $A$ is proper and $B$ separated and finite type, [pqf-lem-image-proper] gives that $I$ is proper and $q$ is proper, in particular quasi-compact. The map $q$ is a homomorphism: composing its multiplication compatibility with the monomorphism $j$ gives the compatibility for $f$, so the two maps to $I$ agree.

The source $A$ is geometrically reduced by [sbc-lem-smooth-geometrically-reduced]. The injection $\mathcal O_I\to q_*\mathcal O_A$ supplied by [lemma-nagata-scheme-image-ideal-qc] makes $q$ scheme-theoretically dominant. Applying [lem-sbc-geometrically-reduced-dominant-descent] to this quasi-compact map shows that $I$ is geometrically reduced. Thus [lem-sfb-geometrically-reduced-group-smooth] makes $I$ smooth. Also $I$ is connected: a nontrivial clopen partition of $I$ would pull back under the continuous surjection $q$ to a nontrivial clopen partition of connected $A$. Properness, smoothness and connectedness give an abelian variety by [def-sc-abelian-variety].

Both $A$ and $I$ are proper by step 1, hence separated and of finite type [def-weil-proper-morphism], so [lem-sfb-algebraic-group-homomorphism-factorization] applies to the homomorphism $q:A\to I$: $q=i'\circ q'$ with $q':A\to I'$ faithfully flat and $i':I'\to I$ a closed immersion. Since $q$ is surjective, so is $i'$. The scheme $I$ is reduced: take $L=k$ in the geometric reducedness [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible] of step 2. By [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-source-factors-through-closed-subscheme], $\mathrm{id}_I$ factors as $i'\circ s$; then $i'\circ s\circ i'=i'$, and as the closed immersion $i'$ is a monomorphism, $s\circ i'=\mathrm{id}_{I'}$, so $i'$ is an isomorphism. Consequently $q=i'\circ q'$ is flat. Let $e_A,e_I$ denote the identity points. The fibre of $q$ over $e_I:\operatorname{Spec}k\to I$ is $K=\ker f$: since $j$ is a monomorphism and $j e_I=e_B$, a map $t:T\to A$ satisfies $qt=e_I$ if and only if $ft=e_B$. This identifies the two fibre products with their identity sections. By [lem-sc-kernel-subgroup], $K$ is a closed subgroup scheme of $A$, hence finite type over $k$.

source.place: Theorem 5.39 (homomorphism theorem), printed p.108, and Proposition 1.70, printed p.28; Remark 5.42 (scheme-theoretic kernel)

proof.text: Apply [lem-sbc-flat-composite-fibre-dimension-at-point] to $A\xrightarrow{q}I\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ at $e_A$. The first morphism is flat by step 3, and both morphisms are locally of finite type since $q$ is proper and $I$ is finite type. The fibres over the sole base point are $A$ and $I$, while the fibre of $q$ over $e_I$ is $K$. Thus, with dimension at a point meaning the minimum of dimensions of its open neighbourhoods, $\dim_{e_A}A=\dim_{e_K}K+\dim_{e_I}I$.

source.place: Remark 5.42, dimension calculation; Stacks Tag 02JS, lemma-dimension-fibre-at-a-point-additive

proof.text: For each $G\in\{A,I,K\}$ the identity is $k$-rational, so its residue field is $k$ and has transcendence degree zero over $k$. The formula [lem-kun-dimension-formula] therefore gives $\dim_{e_G}G=\dim\mathcal O_{G,e_G}$. By [lem-ag-group-identity-local-dimension] this equals $\dim G$. These lemmas apply to all three finite-type group schemes, including the possibly nonreduced $K$. Substitution in step 4 yields $\dim A=\dim K+\dim I=\dim I+\dim K$, as required.

proof_origin.place: Theorem 1.72 and Remark 5.42, with the dimension calculation expanded at the identity using Stacks 02JS and 02FX and the existing group identity dimension theorem
